source_title: Zexyen/Witch-Time: Unofficial static recompilation of Bayonetta 3. Builds the game on your PC from your own legally dumped copy. No game files, keys or SDK code included. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
An unofficial static recompilation of Bayonetta 3 (Nintendo Switch) for PC, in the spirit and architecture of B2recomp : the game's AArch64 code is translated to C on your PC from your own dump , and runs on a re-implemented system layer (threads, file system, input, audio, and NVN on Vulkan). Not an emulator, and not a way to get the game.
This repository contains no game code, no game assets, no Nintendo SDK code, no keys. Everything derived from the game (converted ELFs, translated C, the compiled game.so , caches) is generated locally into targets/ , build/ , cache/ and runtime/gen/ , which git ignores. Never share them.
Details: docs/STATUS.md ; findings: docs/RE_NOTES.md .
A release needs nothing installed but a Vulkan driver and OpenGL ( libGL.so.1 ), which every desktop distribution has: it brings its own compiler (clang + lld in deps/llvm ), the runtime already built ( prebuilt/ , with the FFmpeg it uses) and the build tool. Your PC only translates and compiles the game's code, and that needs no system headers. The deps step checks all of it and names what is missing. Your dump: one folder with exefs/ ( main , sdk , subsdk0 , rtld , main.npdm , plain NSO files) and romfs/ (the .pkz archives and movie/ ), extracted with your own tools from your own console and game; this project decrypts nothing.
A checkout has no prebuilt/ , so the link step builds the runtime too: that needs clang 19 or newer + lld and the development files of SDL3, Vulkan, glslang, FFmpeg and OpenGL. The same happens in a release whose runtime/ you changed ( tools/wtbuild/README.md , "Prebuilt runtime").
The build is one program, wtbuild ( tools/wtbuild , Rust). A release ships it built as build/wtbuild ; in a checkout, build it once with cargo:
Or build the launcher ( launcher/README.md ) and run build/witch-time , which does the same with progress on screen and then plays in its own window.
Setup puts the game data (the dump's romfs ) in targets/romfs , so the Witch Time folder holds the whole game and can be moved anywhere: copied by default (hard links on the same drive, so no extra space, and your dump stays whole), or moved with --move-dump (the launcher's "Move the game data here" switch).
The steps ( deps verify convert mods tables lift compile link text check , resumable; --only , --from , --status ) are those of scripts/setup.py , which stays as the reference the Rust port is checked against ( tools/wtbuild/README.md ). The verify step accepts only the build named in tools/wtbuild/src/setup.rs .
Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. A release ( WitchTime- -windows-x86_64.zip ) needs nothing installed but a Vulkan driver: it brings LLVM's own clang + lld ( deps\llvm ), the runtime already built ( prebuilt\ : witch-time-game.exe , SDL3.dll , ssbu_glslang.dll , FFmpeg's DLLs) and build\wtbuild.exe . Unzip it, run witch-time.exe and pick your dump folder, or:
Windows Defender might flag Witch Time as a Trojan: the release's binaries are not code-signed, and each release has new ones Defender has not seen. Download it only from this repository's Releases page, and check the zip against the .sha256 file beside it ( certutil -hashfile SHA256 ).
Movies play through the FFmpeg that ships in prebuilt\ , in software, so they need no codec on your PC. The album's video clips use Media Foundation, which Windows has; the "N" editions need the Media Feature Pack, and the deps step says so when it is missing. The game runs as build\witch-time-game.exe , with its own window; the launcher waits for it.
Building the runtime yourself (a checkout, or a changed runtime\ ) needs llvm-mingw and the MinGW builds of SDL3, FFmpeg, glslang and the Vulkan headers, named in CPATH and LIBRARY_PATH . CI cross-builds all of it on Linux ( .github/workflows/release.yml , job windows ): wtbuild runtime --target windows --out prebuilt .
Lifter, runtime and build scripts come from B2recomp (K0NL), which builds on ssbu-recomp (Denkishi). GPL-3.0; see NOTICE.md and LICENSE .
The logo's lettering is set in the "Bayonetta" typeface by Kustren (free for non-commercial use), converted to outlines; the font file itself is not included.
Unofficial static recompilation of Bayonetta 3. Builds the game on your PC from your own legally dumped copy. No game files, keys or SDK code included.
